pains.description: How do I get listings in real estate in Dubai? Agents ask how to generate leads, how to find more clients, and how to reach an owner when all they have is a title deed number. With no listings and no leads, a commission-only agent earns nothing.

urgency.evidence: Agents ask how to get listings, generate leads and find more clients in Dubai. Job ads for commission-only agents show that no leads means no pay.
urgency.reasoning: A thin lead flow blocks income now, because agents are paid only when a deal closes. The evidence is four question titles, so how much it hurts is not shown.

who_pays.text: The brokerage pays the portals for listings and pays lead sellers, ad agencies and telesales staff. Commission-only agents pay with unpaid time.
who_pays.reasoning: Job posts show brokerages hiring telesales and lead-generation staff, and portal and lead prices are quoted per listing and per lead. Commission-only job ads show that agents earn only from closed deals.

alternatives.what: Paid listings on Property Finder and Bayut (price per listing)
Verified off-plan buyer leads bought from a lead seller (Dubai Property Leads)
Meta and Google ad campaigns for real estate leads: cost per lead
Lead-generation agency service fee, ad spend paid on top (BM Digital Marketing)
alternatives.price_text: AED 3000 per month, excluding ad spend

alternatives.what: Human substitute: an in-house telecaller or property consultant who finds leads (job ad salary, plus commission)

complaints: Brokers are hit with ad rate hikes, and brokers have hit back at a portal over ad rates.

complaints: A seller's own page says cost per lead is not always predictable.

pains.description: You will never get paid on time. Agents beg for their commission, one agent lost €75k in commission, and a brokerage had to go to court to collect Dh100,000 of unpaid commission. Sellers try to cut out the middleman.

urgency.evidence: An agent lost €75k in commission. A review says agents are never paid on time and must beg for their commission. A court had to order an investor to pay Dh100,000 of unpaid brokerage commission.
urgency.reasoning: The money is already lost or late, so it hurts now. Only two member records show it; the rest are news titles.

who_pays.text: The brokerage and its agents carry the loss. To recover it, they pay lawyers and court fees themselves.
who_pays.reasoning: Commission is the brokerage's only income and the agent's pay. A search result puts lawyer fees for a civil case in Dubai from AED 20,000.

alternatives.what: Human substitute: a Dubai lawyer to bring a civil case, e.g. to recover unpaid commission (lawyer fees at the start)

sellers.name: Co-broke (digital agent-to-agent contracts that secure commission splits)

pains.description: Why I failed in Dubai real estate. New agents struggle to close and quit. Firms hire more brokers, but retention rates remain weak, so they keep re-hiring in a talent war.

urgency.evidence: A first-person video on failing in Dubai real estate. National news says Dubai firms hire more brokers but retention rates remain weak, and that agent failure rates are way too high.
urgency.reasoning: Each agent who fails leaves the floor short, and the firm pays again to hire and license a replacement. Only one member record shows it; the rest are news and recruiter titles.

who_pays.text: The brokerage pays to replace each agent who leaves: the visa, the RERA course and card, and recruiting. Agents who fail pay with months of unpaid time.
who_pays.reasoning: A search result says the employer bears the visa cost under UAE labour law. A recruiter's page and a relocation job post show firms pay to refill the floor.

alternatives.what: RERA training course, exam and broker card for each new agent
Two-year employment visa, medical and Emirates ID for each new agent (the employer pays)

sellers.name: Axe Recruiting (recruits agents for Dubai brokerages)
RERA training institutes (e.g. DX Broker Training)
Sales training for agents (e.g. Innovation Experts Real Estate Institute)

pains.description: The new DLD rule to get Trakheesi: every ad needs a permit. Listings must be updated within 3 days, and sold ones removed. Brokers who break the ad rules are fined: the DLD fined 256 brokers in six months and warns of fines up to Dh50,000.

urgency.evidence: Every ad needs a DLD Trakheesi permit. Listings must be updated within 3 days. The DLD fined 256 brokers in six months and warns brokers to remove illegal ads or face fines up to Dh50,000.
urgency.reasoning: A regulator's rule, enforced with fines, forces action on every listing. The rule is well documented by the DLD and news, but only one member record asks about it.

who_pays.text: The brokerage pays a Trakheesi permit fee for each ad, any DLD fines, and CRM tools that check permit numbers.
who_pays.reasoning: The DLD issues ad permits to licensed brokers and firms and fines both brokers and firms that break the ad rules.
